## 1. Bio-inspired backpropagation-free training for optical neural networks

- Venue: Light Science & Applications, 2026
- Score: 0.88
- Link: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41377-026-02394-3

### Core problem

Traditional optical neural networks rely on error backpropagation, which is incompatible with physical optical systems due to the lack of reciprocal error paths and high sensitivity to fabrication imperfections.

### Method and architecture

The proposed bio-inspired backpropagation-free optical neural network (B-ONN) uses layer-wise target propagation with trainable error convolution kernels. Each layer locally learns from target signals instead of chain-ruled gradients, eliminating the need for precise optical conjugation between forward and backward paths. The architecture was physically validated using a programmable spatial light modulator (SLM) system and further implemented via chip-scale nano printing.

### Main contributions

- Proposes a bio-inspired backpropagation-free optical neural network (B-ONN) that uses layer-wise target propagation and trainable error convolution kernels to enable local learning without gradients.
- Demonstrates B-ONN achieves comparable accuracy to traditional ONNs on MNIST (93.25%) and Fashion-MNIST (82.28%).
- Shows B-ONN has superior robustness against phase noise (75% accuracy at ~0.4π) and alignment errors (75% accuracy within ±3 pixels).
- Physically validates B-ONN using a programmable SLM system (95% accuracy in handwritten digit recognition) and chip-scale nano printing (94% accuracy), confirming transferability from programmable setups to fixed devices.
- Highlights that B-ONN learns smooth phase distributions for inherent structural robustness without noise-augmented training, and its local learning rules support asynchronous parallel updates in scalable deep architectures.

### Reported results

- B-ONN achieves 93.25% accuracy on MNIST and 82.28% on Fashion-MNIST, comparable to traditional ONNs. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- B-ONN demonstrates superior robustness against phase noise (75% accuracy at σ ≈ 0.4π) and alignment errors (75% accuracy within ±3 pixels). (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- Physical validation using a programmable SLM system achieved 95% accuracy in handwritten digit recognition. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- Chip-scale integration via nano printing maintained 94% accuracy. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)

### Research value

This work opens a practical and feasible path for deploying optical computing systems in real-world applications by eliminating the need for backpropagation, demonstrating robustness to fabrication imperfections, and validating transferability from programmable to chip-scale integrated devices.

### Limitations and open questions

- The abstract does not specify the number of layers or network depth tested.
- It is unclear whether the approach scales to larger datasets beyond MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.
- The physical validation uses specific hardware (SLM, nano printing); generalizability to other optical platforms is not discussed.
- Potential limitations in training speed or computational overhead of the target propagation mechanism are not addressed.
- Performance under other noise types (e.g., detector noise) is not mentioned.

## 2. All-optical computing towards 100-GHz clock rates

- Venue: Light Science & Applications, 2026
- Score: 0.85
- Link: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41377-026-02314-5

### Core problem

Conventional processors have clock rates stagnant at ~5 GHz, limiting real-time processing and control of ultrafast information systems.

### Method and architecture

An all-optical recurrent neural network performing linear operations, nonlinear functions, and memory entirely in the optical domain, avoiding electronic bottlenecks.

### Main contributions

- Proposes and experimentally demonstrates all-optical recurrent neural network computing.
- Achieves accuracy surpassing a purely linear model up to 80 GHz clock rates.
- Demonstrates noisy waveform classification task.
- Performs ultrafast in-situ analysis of soliton states from integrated optical microresonators.
- Applies architecture for generative AI using quantum fluctuations to generate images without input optical signals.

### Reported results

- Accuracy surpassing a purely linear model up to 80 GHz clock rates depending on the task. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- Demonstrated a prototypical task of noisy waveform classification. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- Performed ultrafast in-situ analysis of soliton states from integrated optical microresonators. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)
- Illustrated generative AI based on quantum fluctuations to generate images in the absence of input optical signals. (`reported_by_authors`, basis: abstract)

### Research value

Demonstrates potential of all-optical computing beyond digital electronics for ultrafast processing, analysis, and generative tasks.
